name: Strands Agents
summary: AWS’s Apache 2.0 toolkit for building agents in Python and TypeScript: an SDK whose agent is a model, a system prompt and a list of tools run in a loop inside your own process, plus a ready-made harness, sandboxes and evals built on it.
intro: Strands takes what AWS calls a model-driven approach: rather than drawing a workflow, you give the `Agent` a model, a prompt and tools, and the loop lets the model plan. Each turn it sends the conversation and the tool descriptions to the model; if the model asks for a tool, Strands validates the request against the tool’s schema, runs it, appends the result (or the error, so the model can recover) and calls the model again, until the model ends its turn. Any Python function becomes a tool with the `@tool` decorator, whose docstring and type hints are what the model reads; MCP servers plug in as tools through `MCPClient`. Production controls are part of the loop: turn and token budgets, cancellation, stop reasons, hooks on every step, retries, conversation managers that keep history inside the context window, session persistence and OpenTelemetry traces.

Agents run in-process, with no hosted control plane: the docs show deployment to Lambda, Fargate, EKS, EC2, App Runner, Bedrock AgentCore, Docker and Kubernetes. Amazon Bedrock is the default model provider (Claude Sonnet 4.6 in `us-west-2`, using your AWS credentials), and the same agent code runs on Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Ollama, LiteLLM and other providers. Version 1.0 added multi-agent primitives (agents as tools, swarms, graphs) and support for the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol. The SDK, published as `strands-agents` on PyPI and `@strands-agents/sdk` on npm, is now documented as the Strands Harness SDK and lives in the `strands-agents/harness-sdk` repository; Strands harness, released in September 2026, is a fully assembled agent built on it with tuned defaults for prompts, tools, memory and context management.
strengths: Little code for an agent: `Agent(tools=[...])` and a call, with the model, not your code, deciding which tools to use and in what order
Production controls in the box: invocation limits, cancellation, stop reasons, hooks, retries, session persistence and OpenTelemetry tracing
Not tied to one model vendor: Bedrock, Anthropic, OpenAI and Google are first-party providers, plus Ollama, LiteLLM and community packages
Runs inside your own process on any compute, and AWS uses it in production for Amazon Q Developer, AWS Glue and VPC Reachability Analyzer
limits: Defaults lean on AWS: with no model configured it calls Bedrock, so you need AWS credentials and model access enabled, or must pick another provider
Python and TypeScript don’t match: Ollama, LiteLLM, llama.cpp, Mistral and SageMaker are Python-only providers, and Vercel is TypeScript-only
Prompt caching works only where the provider supports cache points (Bedrock, Anthropic, LiteLLM, llama.cpp, Vercel), not with OpenAI, Google or Ollama through Strands

Instructions in the prompt alone aren’t always followed: in a Strands team test over 600 runs, prompt instructions passed 82.5% of the time against 100% with steering hooks, so critical rules belong in hooks or interventions

snippet.title: A custom tool plus a vended tool on the default Bedrock model (pip install strands-agents)
source: def letter_counter(word: str, letter: str) -> int:
"""Count occurrences of a specific letter in a word."""
raise ValueError("The 'letter' parameter must be a single character")
agent('How many letter R\'s are in the word "strawberry"? Write the answer to answer.txt.')

story: Clare Liguori’s team at AWS started building agents for Amazon Q Developer in early 2023, when models weren’t trained to act as agents: getting one to reason and call tools took long prompt instructions, response parsers and orchestration logic, and the agent frameworks that provided that scaffolding meant months of tuning before an agent was ready for production. As models gained native tool use and reasoning, the team found those frameworks getting in the way, so they built a minimal loop instead. An early agent for network troubleshooting was little more than a system prompt, a Claude 3 model and tools.

AWS open-sourced Strands Agents as a preview on 16 May 2025, already used in production by Amazon Q Developer, AWS Glue and VPC Reachability Analyzer, with Anthropic and Meta contributing model providers. Version 1.0 followed on 15 July 2025 with multi-agent primitives, A2A support and a session manager. A TypeScript SDK followed, and by its first anniversary in May 2026 the project counted 25 million downloads. In September 2026 the team released Strands harness, a fully assembled agent on top of what is now called the Strands Harness SDK.

choices.choice: Let the model plan instead of scripting workflows
choices.why: Workflow scaffolding written for one model generation became technical debt when a better model arrived. A prompt plus tools in a loop lets the agent improve with the model without refactoring.
Modeling sub-agents, graphs and swarms as tools lets the model decide when a task needs them, the same way it decides to call any other tool.

choices.choice: Retrieve tools instead of listing them all
choices.why: One internal AWS agent had over 6,000 tools, more than a model can choose from accurately, so Strands showed a pattern where the agent searches a knowledge base for the few tools relevant to the task.

timeline.text: AWS open-sources Strands Agents as a Python SDK preview
Strands Agents 1.0 adds agents-as-tools, graphs, swarms, A2A and remote session storage
Strands harness, a ready-made agent on the Strands Harness SDK, released under Apache 2.0
